turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ag, this computer's stuck on yesterday's file again. One second. Okay, I'm with you. What's been going on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I've been losing weight, and my heart keeps racing, that's really why I came. It's not a checkup, I booked because it's starting to scare me a bit, hey.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm her auntie, I live with her. She's not the same girl these last months, doctor, I'm the one who made her come.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. The weight, say that again, I was clicking the wrong tab. How much have you lost, and since when?

[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): So in January at the gym I was 64 kilos, I'm sure of that, and this morning the scale at home said 58, so six kilos down. I'd put it at two months of proper losing, my work trousers started hanging in March, and I had to buy a belt, which I've never needed.
[SEG0006] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No, it's three months. I remember because it was around my birthday in February that her face looked thinner, so three months, not two.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Auntie, your birthday is the 20th of February and I was still in my old trousers then. The weight went after that. I'm saying two months, I'm not guessing for fun.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay, okay. Somewhere between two and three months, I'll write it that way. Are you eating less to try to lose it?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No, the opposite, that's what freaks me out. I'm eating more than usual, pap in the morning, then I'm starving by tea time, two pies at lunch instead of one, and after supper I'm back in the fridge. I even stopped skipping breakfast on purpose, so this isn't a diet, I promise you.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. And the racing heart, sorry, say it once more, the screen jumped.

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): My heart just goes fast while I'm sitting, err, it thumps in my throat and in my ears, at my desk, not while I'm exercising. My watch has shown numbers over a hundred, like 120, when I've done nothing but type.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The machine in the passage, when we checked in, it read 112. I looked because her hands were shaking too much to trust it.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, 112, I saw it myself. I asked her to read it out because the numbers were bouncing and I didn't want to misread.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): The sister's put 112 on here as well, pulse 112, blood pressure 128 over 76. Fine, I've got it. Any pain in the chest with these episodes?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No pain at all. Not a stitch, not a pressure, nothing like that. I do get a bit short of breath on the stairs at work, one flight and I'm puffing, which didn't used to happen, but there's no pain.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sweats?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Shame, yes. I sweat through a shirt in an air-conditioned office, and at night the sheet is damp and I have to flip the pillow. It's not like a fever sweat, I checked, I just run hot, and it's been with the weight loss the whole time.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And she sleeps badly. I'm the other side of the wall, doctor, she's up and down the passage all night, light on, light off.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not right. I fall asleep without any trouble, I wake once, maybe twice, because I'm sweaty, and then I'm gone again. I'm not pacing the passage, I sleep okay, auntie just hears me open the window.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hands shaking, is that every day?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day, ja. Tea ripples in the mug, and I mistype at work, it's a fine shake in both hands. It's a bit worse if I've gone too long without food, but eating doesn't switch it off, I need to be clear about that, it stays.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She also doesn't take the tablets on Sundays. The propranalol, the little white ones from the GP.

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Not Sundays, auntie, please. I miss Saturdays, because I sleep in and I skip the morning one and then I don't bother with the night one either. Every other day I take them properly, propranolol 10 mg, twice a day, by mouth, doctor Naidoo in Mamelodi started them about three weeks ago for the racing heart.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Propranolol 10 milligrams twice a day, Saturdays off. Any other tablets? The list on the screen is blank and I don't trust it.

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the only one I actually take. Months ago I tried magnesium, two days, a tablet from the chemist, and I stopped because it did nothing, so that's discontinued, don't put it as current. No vitamins, no contraceptive, nothing else.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Her sister is on carbimazole. Just so you know, it's not Thandi's medicine, it's Lindi's.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, my older sister Lindi has thyroid disease, the overactive kind. They diagnosed her about four years ago and she's been on carbimazole since, I don't know the dose and it's not mine. My mother said it can run in the family, which is half the reason I didn't just ignore this.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sister, overactive thyroid, noted. Allergies to any medicine?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none. I had penicillin as a kid for tonsillitis and nothing happened, and the propranolol hasn't given me a rash or a swollen lip or anything, so no known allergies.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bowels? Any diarrhoea with all this eating?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No diarrhoea. Once a day, same as always, normal, I'm sorry for the detail but you asked and I don't want you thinking I'm leaving something out.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you feel hot all the time, or cold?

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Hot. Constantly. Window open at night even when my auntie is in a gown and socks, and at work I'm in a vest while the others have jerseys on. I don't feel cold, not even in the morning.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Eyes? Any bulging, or double vision? Just yes or no if you can.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No bulging, no double vision. This isn't my eyes, I had them tested last year for the screen work and they were fine.

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me look, hands out flat. Ja, fine tremor in both hands, and the skin is warm. Neck now, swallow for me, sorry I glanced at the screen. No goitre, thyroid feels normal.
[SEG0037] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She cut her finger chopping onions last week. It healed in five days, I checked it every night, completely closed.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): So nothing that's slow to heal?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No. That cut was small and it healed in five days, totally normal. I don't get slow-healing wounds.

[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking out loud, so don't quote me as a diagnosis. Losing weight while eating more, sweats, a tremor, pulse of 112, and a sister with thyroid disease, that can be an overactive thyroid, thyrotoxicosis. It can just as easily be anxiety, or caffeine, and I am not concluding either one today.

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I barely have caffeine. One Coke at lunch, no coffee, no energy drinks, I don't like the taste. And I'm not a stressed person, I'm 27 and I do admin at a logistics company in Centurion, four years in October, the job is fine, this isn't worry.

[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): One Coke, job noted. Still not calling it. I'm booking bloods, thyroid function and a full blood count, and an ECG. The ECG is today, the sister at the back will do it before you leave, and the bloods go off this afternoon.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): The ECG is just stickers, right? I had one years ago at varsity when I fainted in a lecture, once, and it was normal, they said, and I never fainted again, I only mention it so you have the whole story, not because it's happening now.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stickers only, no shock. Come back in two weeks, reception will book you, results should be in. That visit is happening either way, not only if something's wrong.
[SEG0045] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She gets very tired as well. Every afternoon she is flat on the couch before supper, I see it, she won't always tell you.

[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, that part is true, I'll give her that. I am tired, a heavy tired from about four o'clock, I still finish my work but I'm done after. The couch is accurate. The sleeping-all-night thing I still don't agree with.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tiredness, got it. No new script today, we wait for the bloods. Sharp, they'll call you for the ECG just now.

spec.situation: Younger adult losing weight with a fast heartbeat, sweating, shaky hands, eats more than usual; hair thinning not mentioned; a sister has thyroid disease; blood tests and ECG planned.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Palpitations were described as thumping in her throat and ears while sitting at her desk, with smartwatch readings over 100 and up to 120 despite doing nothing but typing.
The patient denied trying to lose weight and specifically said this is not due to dieting.
Shortness of breath was specifically denied to be accompanied by chest pain; she said there was 'not a stitch, not a pressure'.
Sweating included night sweats with damp sheets and needing to flip the pillow, and she said she had checked that it was not fever-related.
The patient disputed the caregiver's report of poor sleep, stating she falls asleep easily, wakes once or twice because of sweating, then goes back to sleep and is not pacing the passage.
The hand tremor does not resolve with eating; she specifically said eating does not switch it off.
She denied taking any other current medicines: no vitamins and no contraceptive.
No known drug allergy was supported by history that she tolerated penicillin in childhood and propranolol without rash or lip swelling.
Examination finding omitted/wrongly incomplete: the doctor said the thyroid felt normal, not just that there was no goitre.

Past history/family context omitted: her sister's overactive thyroid was diagnosed about four years ago and treated with carbimazole; the patient said thyroid disease may run in the family per her mother.
The doctor explicitly said he was not concluding a diagnosis today and that the differential could just as easily be anxiety or caffeine as thyrotoxicosis.
The patient rebutted excess caffeine and anxiety as explanations, saying she barely has caffeine and does not consider herself a stressed person.
Past history detail omitted: prior syncope was a single episode years ago at varsity, ECG was reportedly normal, and she has not fainted again; she said this is not happening now.
Follow-up plan detail omitted: the doctor said the two-week review should happen either way, not only if something is wrong.
Management plan omitted: no new prescription was given today; they will wait for the blood results.
